title: Sovereign Principality of the United Netherlands
capsule: The Sovereign Principality of the United Netherlands was established on 2 December 1813 when William Frederick of Orange-Nassau returned from English exile after Napoleon's retreat and was proclaimed Sovereign Prince by a provisional government. A constitution adopted in March 1814 created a centralized state with a unicameral States General, replacing the decentralized structure of the old Dutch Republic. The principality was transitional by design: at the Congress of Vienna the Great Powers agreed to merge the northern Netherlands with the former Austrian Netherlands (Belgium) into a larger state, and on 16 March 1815 William Frederick was crowned King William I of the United Kingdom of the Netherlands, dissolving the principality after barely fifteen months.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The territory corresponds to the well-documented former Batavian Republic, and its boundaries are precisely established by early nineteenth-century diplomatic records; there is no ambiguity about extent.
